title: Portal checkout
description: Checkout, in the two halves that keep the browser out of the money (portal plan P4.1; F15, D2192). The SPA asks the API for a transaction, naming the workspace and the licence terms it accepted; the API creates it at Paddle with the organisation and workspace in its custom_data; and the overlay is opened with the transaction id and nothing else. A page that could name what it was buying could name a victim's workspace, buy against it and refund, which is the finding this split answers. Every object here is closed, because ee/keyservice/wire_checkout.go decodes it with DisallowUnknownFields.

create.description: The SPA's request to start a purchase. The organisation is the caller's membership and not a field: a body that could name one would be a request to bill somebody else.

workspace_id.description: The portal workspace the purchase is for. One active subscription per workspace is the rule (D2192), so this is what the API checks that against before it creates anything.

terms_version.description: The licence terms the buyer accepted (spec §Legal). The version is named rather than a flag being set: a boolean would record that somebody accepted something without recording which wording, and the record has to say which.

session.description: What the SPA opens the Paddle overlay with: one id and nothing else. The price, the quantity and the custom_data are the server's, so a tampered page can at most name a transaction that is not its own, which the overlay and the webhook both refuse.

transaction_id.description: Paddle's id for the transaction the API created. The purchase event that follows is admitted only because a transaction this API created began it (F15).
